hint: I own an HVAC company outside Chicago. We did $1.8M last year with 11 people. We send replacement estimates through Housecall Pro, but too many go quiet. I am still following up from my phone at 9 p.m.
answers: Usually six to ten replacement quotes a week, mostly $9k to $14k jobs. We already have the next-day reminder turned on. After that, it is basically me remembering to call. Melissa runs the office, but she is buried in dispatch and phones. I will open the estimates on Sunday and find somebody we quoted two weeks ago who never heard from us again. I do not think another automatic text is the whole answer.

I want a real person checking in within two business days. Some people are comparing bids, some are trying to get financing, and some just did not understand the options. Those are different conversations. I am not sure our Housecall Pro plan can create those tasks automatically, so please do not build this around a feature we might not have. Right now nobody is clearly responsible once the estimate goes out. Melissa assumes I have it, and I assume she called.

Housecall Pro is where the quotes and customer notes live. We can already pull up sent estimates by date. Melissa uses Outlook for her calendar. I really do not want a second list that somebody has to keep in sync. I could have our dispatcher cover the phones for 20 minutes at 3 on Monday, Wednesday and Friday so Melissa can make calls. She can ask what is holding someone up and book a callback with me. She cannot change pricing or make promises about an install date.

We can put that in the estimate notes today. I do not know about custom fields, and I do not want to spend a week figuring them out. There are 18 open replacement estimates right now, so she cannot call everybody in one 20-minute block. I want her to handle routine follow-up and bring me the pricing or technical questions in one batch. I could review that batch Tuesday and Friday morning. What would you actually have us do Monday, and how would we tell after two weeks whether this is working?

I am not sold on eighteen separate Outlook tasks. That sounds like another admin job for Melissa, and she is already swamped. Also, all three steps say start Monday, so what is the actual one change? She has 20 minutes and 18 estimates. Which ones does she call first, what does she say, and where does she leave the next step so I am not back in there Sunday? Keep it inside Housecall Pro notes and the three calendar blocks we already agreed on.

Melissa can send the batch. But our baseline is not zero follow-ups; I already make some of these calls myself. And a note saying no question does not tell us whether somebody wants financing, bought elsewhere, or just did not answer. I want a useful outcome and a dated next step, not a tick saying we called. Please revise the plan around that one 20-minute routine. Include a normal-sounding opening Melissa can use, what stays with her versus comes to me Tuesday or Friday, and a two-week check that tells me whether fewer quotes are being forgotten and whether I am getting my evenings back.

Hang on, you put the individual Outlook reminders back in after I said that was too much admin. And the revised plan still does not give Melissa an opening she can actually say on the phone. I am trying to hand this off, not spend another evening rewriting the instructions. Give me the plain-English version I can tell her Monday morning: who she calls first, what she asks, what she writes down, and when something comes to me. No extra reminders or new tools.
